note: This package merges TWO Braids shapes (SQUARE_SUB, SAW_SUB), so every case sets its own "shape" key rather than relying on a top-level default. p1 (TIMBRE, macro_oscillator.cc:230) drives the main oscillator's own shape parameter -- pulse width for SQUARE_SUB (analog_oscillator.cc:206), saw-shape for SAW_SUB (analog_oscillator.cc:354) -- and maps to the engine's TIMBRE. p2 (COLOR, macro_oscillator.cc:236-249) drives both the sub's octave choice and its blend level and maps to the engine's MORPH. HARMONICS is the port's own continuous stand-in for Braids' discrete shape switch, so it is pinned to 0.0 (SQUARE_SUB) or 1.0 (SAW_SUB) per case rather than swept. MACRO has no Braids equivalent (Braids' sub is a fixed 50% square, macro_oscillator.cc:234-235) and sits at 0.5 in every case but `square-macro-max`, which checks the other end of ApplyMacro's stock plateau. TOLERANCE POLICY: every case declares the SAME baseline -- acRmsDb 1.0, spectrumDb 1.0, cents 2.0 -- so a deviation fails and stays visible instead of being absorbed by a per-case widening. Two cases omit `cents` rather than widen it, because the f0 estimator is degenerate there on BOTH sides (it returns its own f_max boundary, 2000.0 Hz, for reference and port alike, so the metric measures nothing); that is stated per case. 10 of the 18 cases fail, 18 individual breaches; every failure belongs to one of the three DSP deviations declared in the engine header (the pulse-width law, SAW_SUB's inert TIMBRE, the DC blocker's corner), and each case's note carries its measured figures.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, TIMBRE 0.88 (where the pw law first breaks 1 dB)
cases.note_case: Bounds the pulse-width deviation from below. MEASURED +1.11 dB AC RMS / 1.51 dB spectrum, so the deviation spans roughly the top 12% of TIMBRE's travel, not the top 2%. Below this it stays inside the baseline: +0.44 dB / 0.79 dB at TIMBRE 0.75, +0.11 dB / 0.43 dB at 0.5.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, TIMBRE 0.977 (Braids' clamp knee -- the WORST point)
cases.note_case: The pulse-width law's worst disagreement is HERE, not at TIMBRE 1.0. Braids' low fraction is (32768 - min(p1*32767, 32000)) / 65536: it falls at ~0.5 - 0.5*p1 until parameter_ meets the 32000 clamp at p1 = 0.9766, then holds at 0.01172. The port's `pw = 0.5 - 0.48*timbre` (sub_oscillator_engine.cc) keeps falling to 0.02. At p1 = 0.977 the port's pulse is 0.0310 against Braids' 0.0117 -- 2.6x wider, the largest ratio anywhere on the axis. MEASURED +4.44 dB AC RMS / 5.13 dB spectrum, roughly double the TIMBRE=1.0 case below.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, TIMBRE at maximum (thinnest pulse)
cases.note_case: MEASURED +2.56 dB AC RMS / 2.98 dB spectrum. This is NOT the worst point (see square-timbre-knee) and it is NOT caused by Braids' 32000 clamp: at TIMBRE 0.95, comfortably below the clamp threshold of 0.9766, the port is already +2.53 dB out. The cause is the port's 0.48 coefficient against Braids' effective ~0.5, which makes the port's pulse proportionally wider the narrower the pulse gets. Excess predicted from duty alone -- 20*log10 of the sqrt(pw*(1-pw)) ratio -- is +0.11 dB at TIMBRE 0.5, +0.42 at 0.75, +1.25 at 0.9, +4.14 at 0.977 and +2.28 at 1.0, each within ~0.2 dB of measurement, so the coefficient explains the whole axis.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, TIMBRE swept 0 -> 1 across the render
cases.note_case: The whole axis under motion, as one number. MEASURED -0.35 dB AC RMS / 1.70 dB spectrum: the level error integrates away, the spectral error does not. Static endpoints alone would have missed that.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, both knobs centred, note 84
cases.note_case: The control for square-timbre-max-high-note: MEASURED +0.18 dB AC RMS / 0.40 dB spectrum. Whatever fails at note 84 below is the pulse-width floor, not a pitch or rate error.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, TIMBRE at maximum, note 84
cases.note_case: PITCH IS AN AXIS FOR THIS ENGINE, because the port's pulse-width floor moves with it and Braids' does not. VariableShapeOscillator::Render CONSTRAINs pw to [2f, 1-2f] (variable_shape_oscillator.h:107-111), f being the normalized frequency; AnalogOscillator::RenderSquare has no such term -- it clamps only parameter_. At note 84, 2f = 0.0437, so the port's narrowest pulse is 3.7x wider than Braids' 0.0117 and TIMBRE's own law is not in control of it at all. The crossover is around MIDI 61, where 2f first exceeds Braids' floor; around MIDI 71 the CONSTRAIN also overrides the port's own 0.02 floor. MEASURED +8.35 dB AC RMS / 5.04 dB spectrum, with the f0 estimator reading 1045 Hz for Braids against 262 Hz for the port.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, MORPH fully down (sub two octaves down, max blend)
cases.note_case: Also the check that the sub really is 24 semitones down: the f0 estimator locks the sub at 27.5007 Hz for Braids and 27.5729 Hz for the port, a raw +4.54 cents, which is exactly the kCorrectedSampleRate offset the harness subtracts -- so the octave constant is exact.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, MORPH fully up (sub one octave down, max blend)
SQUARE_SUB, COLOR swept 0 -> 1 (both blend ramps and the octave switch)
cases.note_case: The one case that exercises MORPH as a continuum rather than at three points: both legs of the V, and the octave crossover at the centre. It also probes the one thing Braids does here that the port does not -- BEGIN_INTERPOLATE_PARAMETER_1 smooths the sub gain WITHIN each 24-sample block (macro_oscillator.cc:242-249) while the port applies `blend` at block rate. MEASURED +0.01 dB AC RMS / 0.41 dB spectrum, so at Braids' block size the missing smoothing does not register.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, MORPH fully down, note 24 (sub at 8.2 Hz)
cases.note_case: The DC blocker's real cost, which Braids does not pay because it has no blocker. The 0.999 pole puts the corner at (1 - 0.999) * 47872.34 / 2pi = 7.6 Hz. At note 24 -- an ordinary bass note -- the two-octave sub lands at 8.18 Hz, 1.07x the corner rather than an order of magnitude above it, and the blocker takes 2.7 dB and 43 degrees off it. MEASURED -1.11 dB AC RMS / 0.83 dB spectrum. Even the note-45 cases clear the corner by only 3.6x (sub 27.5 Hz), where the cost is 0.32 dB. `cents` is omitted: the f0 estimator returns its own f_max boundary (2000.0 Hz) for BOTH sides here, so the metric measures nothing and a tolerance on it would be theatre.

cases.name: SQUARE_SUB, MACRO at maximum (the far end of ApplyMacro's stock plateau)
cases.note_case: MACRO cannot be A/B'd as an axis -- Braids has no equivalent control -- but its STOCK PLATEAU can be, and this is the check that the plateau is really flat. ApplyMacro(0.5, 0.12, 0.5, macro) has maximum == stock, so everything from the detent up should be Braids exactly. Verified two ways: this case measures identically to square-morph-low-octave (-0.10 dB AC RMS / 0.31 dB spectrum), and the port's rendered OUT and AUX at macro 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0 are bit-identical (max abs sample difference 0 on both channels). MACRO 0.0 does move it (-0.81 dB / 2.06 dB against Braids), so the control is live rather than dead.

cases.name: SAW_SUB, both knobs centred
cases.note_case: TIMBRE 0.5 puts Braids' RenderVariableSaw pw at ~0.25, and its naive waveform is `(phase_>>18) + ((phase_-pw)>>18)` (analog_oscillator.cc:414-415) -- two ramps a quarter cycle apart, a genuine two-segment shape. The port renders a plain naive ramp here regardless of TIMBRE. MEASURED +3.57 dB AC RMS / 1.32 dB spectrum.

cases.name: SAW_SUB, TIMBRE at minimum
cases.note_case: THIS END IS WRONG TOO, and the aggregate number nearly hides it. Braids clamps parameter_ to a 1024 minimum (analog_oscillator.cc:344-346), so pw floors at 1024/65536 = 0.015625 rather than zero. The two ramps then sit 1/64 cycle apart, which puts a comb null on harmonic 32 (3520 Hz at note 45) and on its odd multiples. The port has no such null. MEASURED 1.28 dB spectrum overall, but the per-band breakdown (`--bands`) reads +10.94 dB at 2560-5120 Hz and +3.33 dB at 1280-2560 Hz. Do not read this case as 'TIMBRE happens to work at the bottom'.

cases.name: SAW_SUB, TIMBRE at maximum
cases.note_case: Braids' pw here is ~0.5, so its two ramps sit half a cycle apart and the waveform becomes two near-equal ramps per nominal cycle -- an octave-up shape, which is why the estimator reads Braids at 220.0 Hz against the port's unchanged 110.3 Hz ramp. MEASURED +6.01 dB AC RMS / -1200 cents / 1.57 dB spectrum. Paired with saw-timbre-min: at HARMONICS=1.0 the engine's waveshape (1.0 - 0.5*harmonics) is exactly 0.5, VariableShapeOscillator's pure-saw point, where square_amount and triangle_amount (variable_shape_oscillator.h:137-138) are both exactly zero -- so ComputeNaiveSample returns `phase` untouched and the pw-dependent BLEP corrections (lines 186-189) are scaled by those same zeros. pw, which carries TIMBRE, has no path to the output. Direct confirmation: the port's renders at TIMBRE 0.0 and TIMBRE 1.0 differ by a mean abs sample value of 5.9e-6, and past the first ~2700 samples by at most 1 LSB (-110 dBFS).

cases.name: SAW_SUB, MORPH fully down (sub two octaves down, max blend)
cases.note_case: MORPH itself is correct here -- it is the SAW_SUB main oscillator underneath that still mismatches. `cents` is OMITTED rather than widened: the f0 estimator returns its own f_max boundary (2000.0 Hz) for BOTH the reference and the port, so the raw delta is exactly 0 and the harness's fixed 4.61-cent kCorrectedSampleRate correction turns a non-measurement into a plausible-looking '-4.6 cents'. Widening the cents tolerance here would be dressing up a metric that never ran.

cases.name: SAW_SUB, MORPH fully up (sub one octave down, max blend)
